items.title: 18 NCLT Benches holding half-day sittings due to member shortage: Bar Association to Supreme Court
items.summary: The NCLT Bar Association has moved the Supreme Court claiming that at least 18 benches of the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) are holding only half-day sittings because of shortage of members. The Association has filed an intervention application in the Supreme Court's suo motu case concerning the appointment of judicial and technical members and inadequate infrastructure at the NCLT. According to the application, the sanctioned strength of the NCLT continues to be 63 members even though its jurisdiction substantially expanded after the enactment of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC). As of June 30, 2026, the tribunal has 26 judicial members and 25 technical members, including the President, the plea stated The Association said that vacancies arising upon the retirement or completion of tenure of members often remain unfilled, leaving several benches operating at reduced capacity. “ The Tribunal is plagued by chronic vacancies, forcing numerous Benches to function with fewer Members .” The plea added that such vacancies were contributing to delays and mounting case arrears. items.title: New bench, old battle: Maratha reservation case to be reheard for third time by Bombay High Court
items.summary: The legal challenge to Maharashtra’s 2024 Maratha reservation law will be reheard for a third time by the Bombay High Court starting October 9. The challenge to the Act was earlier heard by a bench led by then Acting Chief Justice RV Ghuge . However following his elevation as the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court, a new bench has been formed which will now hear the matter afresh. The new bench is now headed by Justice MS Karnik ; Justices NJ Jamadar and SV Marne who were part of the earlier bench have been retained on the new bench. Justices NJ Jamadar, MS Karnik and SV Marne The bench will start hearing the petitions from October 9. It is a complete reset of the final arguments after almost 20 sittings, which began in June 2025. The Maharashtra State Reservation for Socially and Educationally Backward Classes (SEBC) Act, 2024 grants 10 percent reservation to the Maratha community in education and public employment. The challenge to this Act has faced continuous procedural resets.
